name: ASIS (Anterior Superior Iliac Spine)
clinicalNote: Key bony reference for ALT reference line (ASIS to superolateral patella), DIEP lateral taper, SIEA course, and SCIA/SCIP groin flap.

name: PSIS (Posterior Superior Iliac Spine)
clinicalNote: Primary proximal reference for SGAP perforator mapping (upper-to-middle third junction of line from PSIS to greater trochanter).

name: Iliac Crest (Superior Lateral Rim)
clinicalNote: Key bony reference for DCIA iliac crest osteocutaneous flap, internal oblique harvest, and inferior attachment of latissimus dorsi.

name: Pubic Tubercle
clinicalNote: Medial anchor of inguinal ligament; marks inferior incision limit for DIEP/TRAM and proximal reference for gracilis and pudendal flaps.

name: Greater Trochanter of Femur
clinicalNote: Lateral proximal femoral prominence; distal endpoint of the PSIS–greater trochanter line for SGAP mapping and TFL flap reference.

name: Umbilicus
clinicalNote: Surface midline landmark on skin envelope (L3–L4 disc level); periumbilical zone within 3–4 cm lateral and inferior harbors dominant DIEP perforators.

name: Superolateral Patella
clinicalNote: Distal endpoint of the ASIS–superolateral patella line; dominant ALT perforator B clusters within a 3 cm radius of the midpoint.

name: Fibular Head
clinicalNote: Common peroneal nerve courses around the fibular neck; preserve 6–8 cm of proximal fibula during free fibula osteocutaneous harvest.

name: Lateral Malleolus
clinicalNote: Preserve 6–8 cm of distal fibula for ankle mortise stability; reverse sural neurocutaneous flap pivot lies ~5 cm proximal.

name: Medial Epicondyle of Humerus
clinicalNote: Medial reference at the elbow for ulnar artery perforator, radial forearm proximal pedicle course, and medial arm flap landmarks.

name: Acromion
clinicalNote: Lateral shoulder bony anchor for deltopectoral, pectoralis major, supraclavicular, and lateral arm flap axis orientation.

name: Inferior Angle of Scapula
clinicalNote: Superior border of latissimus dorsi crosses the scapular tip; parascapular and scapular angular branch flaps center around this landmark.

name: Mastoid Process
clinicalNote: Key cranial base bony landmark for sternocleidomastoid, temporoparietal fascia, occipital/trapezius, and lateral neck flap orientation.
